title: Money
description: Class 4 IMO — Money: multiplying and dividing money for unit price and total cost, basic profit and loss, making bills, calculating change, and simple budget problems.

topics.title: Unit Price & Total Cost
topics.concept:
The price of one item is the unit price. To find the total cost, multiply the unit price by the quantity: 6 pens at ₹15 each cost 6 × ₹15 = ₹90.

To find the unit price from a total, divide: ₹100 for 5 items means ₹100 ÷ 5 = ₹20 each.

examples.problem: Find the cost of 4 pens at ₹12 each.
3 toys cost ₹150 in total. What is the price of one toy?

quiz.q: What is the cost of 5 books at ₹40 each?
₹120 is paid for 4 toys. What is the price of one toy?

topics.title: Profit & Loss (Basic)
topics.concept: The price a shopkeeper pays is the cost price (CP) and the price they sell at is the selling price (SP). If SP is more than CP, there is a profit = SP − CP. If SP is less than CP, there is a loss = CP − SP.

examples.problem: An item is bought for ₹50 and sold for ₹65. Profit or loss?
An item is bought for ₹80 and sold for ₹70. Profit or loss?

recap: Profit = SP − CP (when SP is more).
Loss = CP − SP (when SP is less).

quiz.q: A toy is bought for ₹100 and sold for ₹120. What is the profit?
A bag is bought for ₹200 and sold for ₹180. What is the loss?

topics.title: Bills, Change & Budget
topics.concept: A bill is the total of all item costs. The change is the money paid minus the bill. A budget is the money you plan to spend — subtract what you spend to see what is left.

examples.problem: Items cost ₹45, ₹30 and ₹25. You pay ₹200. What is the change?
Your budget is ₹500 and you spend ₹350. How much is left?

recap: Bill = sum of all item costs.
Change = amount paid − bill; budget left = budget − spent.

quiz.q: A bill is ₹125 + ₹75. You pay ₹500. What is the change?
Your budget is ₹1,000 and you spend ₹650. How much is left?

questions.q: If 1 pen costs ₹10, then 10 pens cost ___ ?
In which case is there a profit?
questions.explanation: Profit happens when SP is more than CP, which is true only in the first case.
